topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the scope of the lecture series, and presents the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer development, etiology, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous genetic mutations and random chance with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on the specific etiology and chromosomal translocation mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts, transversions, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between tumor initiation and promotion, demonstrating how chronic inflammation, signaling agonists, and developmental timing drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Approaches to identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing the main takeaways on environmental carcinogenesis and risk appraisal.
